error.description: A sample of a mistake with an occurrence count, minted by the reporter so resends land once.

hits.description: Occurrences represented by this sample; omitted means one.

level.description: What it cost the caller. A warning is a failure near its line, such as a press a little past its budget: it opens no bug, and the daily digest's chart counts it.

message.description: The failure sentence when nothing was thrown.

fault.description: An explicit group key, otherwise computed downstream.

bug.description: The group written by the grouper.

commit.description: The commit sha of the running code.

version.description: The app version that produced the error.

tags.description: Additional catch context; never request headers, cookies or bodies.

during.description: What an error happened among, by global eid.

entity.description: The call, effect, entry or process being run, or the signed-in person whose browser opened a document.

session.description: The session whose work raised the error.

process.description: The process when the entity does not already name it.

kind.description: The served entity’s kind, read where it happened.

breadcrumbs.description: The last twenty page navigations, API calls and console errors.

exception.description: The tracker’s stack, parsed frames and catch mechanism for a thrown value.

stack.description: The stack trace, as the runtime reported it.

cause.description: What the error was wrapped around: each `cause` down its chain, its name and message, then its stack.

mechanism.description: The hook that caught the throw.

probe.description: An occurrence sent to prove the path from a reporter to grouping, as a deploy's canary is. Grouping writes its receipt and files it under no bug.

grouped.description: When grouping reached it: the receipt its sender reads.

regressed.description: A resolved bug that happened again after its resolution, in code that had not produced it before or naming no release at all.

error.description: The occurrence that brought the bug back.

message.description: What that occurrence said, which the bug's title, its first occurrence's, does not.

taken.description: A fixer started on the bug. Written again when a fixer takes it after a regression.

task.description: The work item, by the name the graph working on it gives it (T-123).

archived.description: A bug set aside without a fix, by whoever archived it. Nothing archives a bug on its own: a task's state never does.

reason.description: Why it was archived, such as the person's own app code having broken.

resolved.description: How a bug was fixed, as the agent that fixed its cause and saw the fix live explained it. Nothing resolves a bug on its own: one that stopped stays open. The tracker refuses a bug's resolution without its cause and recur.

broke.description: What broke and whom it reached, in plain words for someone who never saw the error.

since.description: The commit that introduced it, by its full sha, when known.

fix.description: The commit that fixed it, by its full sha.

recur.description: Whether it can happen again, and why.

error_group.description: Group each ungrouped occurrence, atomically counting and linking it, then trim its bug to the newest hundred occurrences and the first of each commit or version; a probe gets its receipt and no bug.

digest.description: Marks the recurring wake that sends the daily bug digest (./digest.ts).

bug_digest.description: Send the daily digest of bugs, once a day: new, fixed with time to fix, still open and who is on each, and which reached a person, above a chart of the last two weeks.

bug_settle.description: Archive, in a space's tracker, the reports of a person's app that a resolved bug's occurrences stand for, and resolve with the resolution's explanation a bug of the space's they leave with no open occurrence, so its owner and Operator stop hearing of a break yaks.app fixed; and hand each space whose Operator conversations the bug stopped (occurrences tagged rerun) the faults they were filed under, so it runs them again.

bug_list.title: List bugs
bug_list.description: List bugs, open by default. Answers source-labelled rows as text and output.value for either store. For yaks.app, every tracker's: the platform's, then each space's, whose rows name the space in $scope, the scope bug_show and the marks take; a space tracker that could not be read is said in unread.

query.description: A yaks query, .bug.status=open by default. The yaks.app trackers keep no search index and refuse bare words: match a property instead, as .doc.title~=exists.

limit.description: How many to read from each tracker, at most 100; 50 by default.

source.description: Read box bugs (this graph's, or the box tracker's graph the config names), or the platform tracker on yaks.app; the default is the configured source, box unless the config names yaks.app (as the box's default yak does, beside admin_errors). Reads return source-labelled data without importing bundles.

bug_show.title: Show bugs
bug_show.description: Read a bug, its marks and its newest retained occurrences in full, with the requests they ran during. Answers source-labelled rows, occurrences (how many it retains) and, where older ones remain, next: pass it as after to read the next page. Text and output.value for either store.

bug.description: Box bug id or title; for yaks.app, the bug’s global eid or the hex it starts with (4fde03f7).

limit.description: How many occurrences to read, newest first; 5 by default.

after.description: The next a previous answer named: reads the occurrences older than it.

scope.description: For yaks.app, the global eid of the space whose tracker holds the bug, as bug_list names it in $scope and a space tracker's letter in its link (scope=…); the platform tracker by default.

source.description: Read box bugs (this graph's, or the box tracker's graph the config names), or the platform tracker on yaks.app; the default is the configured source, box unless the config names yaks.app (as the box's default yak does, beside admin_errors). Reads return source-labelled data without importing bundles.

bug_resolve.title: Resolve bugs
bug_resolve.description: Mark a bug fixed, once its fix is live, explained: what broke and whom it reached, why, the commits that introduced and fixed it, and whether it can come back. Resolve only a bug whose cause you fixed and saw live; one that stopped, went quiet or passed on a rerun stays open until its cause is found and fixed. Box marks reach the configured remote tracker before the local mark; yaks.app marks the platform tracker, or the space tracker its scope names.

bug.description: Box bug id or title; for yaks.app, the bug’s global eid or the hex it starts with (4fde03f7).

source.description: Mark box bugs (this graph's, or the box tracker's graph the config names), including their remote copy when configured, or the platform tracker on yaks.app; the default is the configured source, box unless the config names yaks.app (as the box's default yak does, beside admin_errors).

scope.description: For yaks.app, the global eid of the space whose tracker holds the bug, as bug_list names it in $scope and a space tracker's letter in its link (scope=…); the platform tracker by default.

broke.description: What broke and whom it reached, in plain words for someone who never saw the error: a sentence or two.

cause.description: Why it broke: a sentence or two.

since.description: The sha of the commit that introduced it, when known; a short one is read as Git reads it.

fix.description: The sha of the commit that fixed it, live; a short one is read as Git reads it. A fix that is not a commit (a key put in the vault, a row repaired) is said in cause.

recur.description: Whether it can happen again, and why.

bug_archive.title: Archive bugs
bug_archive.description: Hide a bug without discarding occurrences, saying why: an archived bug is one someone set aside, never fixed. Archiving closes its task; a task's own state never marks its bug. Box marks reach the configured remote tracker before the local mark; yaks.app marks the platform tracker, or the space tracker its scope names.

bug.description: Box bug id or title; for yaks.app, the bug’s global eid or the hex it starts with (4fde03f7).

reason.description: Why it is archived, in a sentence for the owner, such as which app's own code broke and how.

source.description: Mark box bugs (this graph's, or the box tracker's graph the config names), including their remote copy when configured, or the platform tracker on yaks.app; the default is the configured source, box unless the config names yaks.app (as the box's default yak does, beside admin_errors).

scope.description: For yaks.app, the global eid of the space whose tracker holds the bug, as bug_list names it in $scope and a space tracker's letter in its link (scope=…); the platform tracker by default.

bug_reopen.title: Reopen bugs
bug_reopen.description: Take a bug's resolution back, so it is open again until an agent fixes its cause: for one resolved without a fix, such as one that only stopped. Its occurrences and its thread stay as they are, and a bug whose opening was told is not told again. Box marks reach the configured remote tracker before the local mark; yaks.app marks the platform tracker, or the space tracker its scope names.

bug.description: Box bug id or title; for yaks.app, the bug’s global eid or the hex it starts with (4fde03f7).

source.description: Mark box bugs (this graph's, or the box tracker's graph the config names), including their remote copy when configured, or the platform tracker on yaks.app; the default is the configured source, box unless the config names yaks.app (as the box's default yak does, beside admin_errors).

scope.description: For yaks.app, the global eid of the space whose tracker holds the bug, as bug_list names it in $scope and a space tracker's letter in its link (scope=…); the platform tracker by default.

tracker_retry.title: Retry the platform tracker's failed runs
tracker_retry.description:
Put the platform tracker's failed effect runs on yaks.app back to pending with a fresh attempt allowance, once the fix for what failed them is live, so the tracker works them again within seconds and the fix is seen to work: a bug's settling (bug_settle), its frames (error_frames), its letters. Takes a handler name for all its failed runs, or one run's id, and says how many it put back. A run that fails again is left failed again. The box tracker's own runs are retried with effect_retry in its graph.

  yak tracker retry bug_settle

of.description: a handler name (all its failed runs) or one run's id

tracker_drop.title: Drop the platform tracker's runs no one owes
tracker_drop.description:
Delete the platform tracker's effect runs on yaks.app that no one owes any more: failed runs, and pending runs whose handler the tracker no longer declares, such as those a release stopped running. Takes a handler name for all such runs, or one run's id, and says how many it deleted. The box tracker's own runs are dropped with effect_drop in its graph.

  yak tracker drop error_trim

of.description: a handler name (all its failed or orphaned runs) or one run's id

error_frames.description: Resolve grouped stack frames through the code catalog without recounting occurrences; unavailable catalogs defer the recorded run until they answer.

merged.description: An entity consolidated into another; its issued address still names the survivor.

bug.description: A group of tracked errors with the same fault, scoped to an app.

app.description: The app, absent for platform and box bugs.

spot.description: The unresolved file, line and function.

hits.description: Occurrences grouped, including those retained only in the count.

days.description: Its hits by day, YYYY-MM-DD, for the last thirty days; a quiet day is absent.

people.description: Distinct people its retained occurrences reached, by their user_id tag.

account.description: person when any retained occurrence reached a person or a person's space, test when every one it names is a test account; absent when none names one.
